title: Error handling and transactions in Fabric Warehouse and SQL analytics endpoint
summary: TRY...CATCH works, and so do ERROR_NUMBER, ERROR_MESSAGE, ERROR_SEVERITY, ERROR_STATE, ERROR_PROCEDURE, @@ERROR, @@TRANCOUNT, @@ROWCOUNT and ROWCOUNT_BIG. ERROR_LINE, XACT_STATE, FORMATMESSAGE and @@PROCID are rejected. One such call anywhere in a batch or procedure stops the whole thing from compiling, including code inside a CATCH block that never runs. Use @@TRANCOUNT instead of XACT_STATE to decide on ROLLBACK, and build messages with CONCAT. Transactions run under snapshot isolation only.

claims.statement: ERROR_LINE is not supported in Fabric. Logging code that captures the failing line number will not compile.
claims.sql_server: SQL Server supports ERROR_LINE inside a CATCH block.
claims.alternative: Drop the line number. Record a step label of your own and ERROR_PROCEDURE() in the log row instead.

claims.statement: Putting ERROR_LINE inside a CATCH block still fails the whole batch at compile time, even if the TRY block never errors. A copied SQL Server CATCH template breaks the entire procedure.
claims.probe_sql: BEGIN TRY SELECT 1 AS a; END TRY BEGIN CATCH SELECT ERROR_NUMBER() AS n, ERROR_LINE() AS l; END CATCH
claims.sql_server: In SQL Server this batch compiles and runs.
claims.alternative: Remove ERROR_LINE from CATCH templates. Keep ERROR_NUMBER, ERROR_MESSAGE, ERROR_SEVERITY, ERROR_STATE and ERROR_PROCEDURE.

claims.statement: XACT_STATE is not supported. The usual 'IF XACT_STATE() <> 0 ROLLBACK' line in a CATCH block fails to compile.
claims.probe_sql: BEGIN TRY SELECT 1 AS a; END TRY BEGIN CATCH IF XACT_STATE() <> 0 ROLLBACK; END CATCH
claims.sql_server: SQL Server supports XACT_STATE, which returns 1, 0 or -1.
claims.alternative: Use IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK; in the CATCH block.

claims.statement: @@TRANCOUNT is supported and returns int. It is the way to test for an open transaction in Fabric.
The Fabric-safe CATCH pattern compiles: roll back when @@TRANCOUNT > 0, then rethrow with a bare THROW.
claims.probe_sql: BEGIN TRY SELECT 1 AS a; END TRY BEGIN CATCH IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK; THROW; END CATCH

claims.statement: ERROR_NUMBER, ERROR_SEVERITY and ERROR_STATE are supported and return int.
claims.probe_sql: SELECT ERROR_NUMBER() AS n, ERROR_SEVERITY() AS s, ERROR_STATE() AS st

claims.statement: ERROR_MESSAGE is supported and returns nvarchar(4000).
ERROR_PROCEDURE is supported and returns nvarchar(128). Use it to identify where the error happened.
@@PROCID is not supported. The logging habit OBJECT_NAME(@@PROCID) fails to compile.
claims.alternative: Use ERROR_PROCEDURE() in CATCH, or hard-code the procedure name as a literal.

claims.statement: FORMATMESSAGE is not supported, so it cannot build THROW or RAISERROR message text.
claims.sql_server: SQL Server supports FORMATMESSAGE with printf-style arguments.
claims.alternative: Build the text with CONCAT into a variable, then pass that variable to THROW.

claims.statement: A batch with RAISERROR('...', 16, 1) placed before its SELECT cannot have its result set described: sp_describe_first_result_set returns error 11530 ('no code paths that reach the end of the batch'). The analyser treats a severity-16 RAISERROR as ending that code path, so tools that describe result sets fail on such a batch.
claims.alternative: Do not put an unconditional RAISERROR or THROW ahead of the statement that returns the result set; raise errors inside a CATCH block or a conditional branch. Prefer THROW 50001, 'message', 1; for new code.

claims.statement: @@ROWCOUNT (int) and ROWCOUNT_BIG (bigint) are supported. Use ROWCOUNT_BIG for large loads to avoid int overflow.
claims.probe_sql: SELECT ROWCOUNT_BIG() AS rb, @@ROWCOUNT AS r

claims.statement: @@ERROR is supported and returns int. As in SQL Server, it is reset by every statement, so read it right after the statement you are checking.

Fabric transactions run under snapshot isolation only. A SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL statement asking for another level does not give that level. Code that relies on locking (SERIALIZABLE, READ UNCOMMITTED) can return different results without any error.
claims.probe_sql: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE; SELECT 1 AS a
claims.sql_server: SQL Server honours all isolation levels, and READ COMMITTED is the default.
claims.alternative: Design for snapshot semantics: expect write-write conflicts to fail the later transaction, and retry it.
